title: Category of objects with an isomorphism from their image under an endofunctor
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and $T:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ a functor. The *category of $T$-fixed pairs* $\mathcal C^{T}$ has as objects the pairs $(X,\theta)$ with $X$ an object of $\mathcal C$ and $\theta:T(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ an isomorphism of $\mathcal C$. A morphism $(X,\theta)\to(X',\theta')$ is a morphism $u:X\to X'$ of $\mathcal C$ such that

$$
 u\circ\theta=\theta'\circ T(u):T(X)\longrightarrow X'.
$$

Identities and composition are those of $\mathcal C$ (the composite of two such morphisms satisfies the condition, by functoriality of $T$). The *forgetful functor* $\operatorname{For}:\mathcal C^T\to\mathcal C$ sends $(X,\theta)$ to $X$ and $u$ to $u$; it is faithful. Equivalently, $\mathcal C^T$ is the full subcategory of the category of $T$-algebras (pairs $(X,\theta)$ with $\theta:T(X)\to X$ arbitrary, same morphisms) on the pairs whose structure map $\theta$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Deligne, La conjecture de Weil II, (1.1.14), p. 153 (the category of sheaves $\mathcal F$ on $X$ with an isomorphism $F^*:F^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F$, for $T=F^*$); the general construction is category theory
